newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares extend gains, seen down on Friday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares extend gains, seen down on Friday.

text.p: Polish shares rose for the sixth session running but analysts said the strong selling after fixing signalled a fall on Friday despite Thursday's high turnover caused by strong demand for copper firm KGHM.
KGHM Polska Miedz SA started trade at 23.5 zlotys ($7.1), 11.9 percent above its institutional-investor issue price.

"The recent growth was likely linked with hopes that money invested in KGHM would return to the market, which has probably happened to a degree, but it seems the extra demand was too short-term and small to lift prices significantly," said Dariusz Szepieniec, an analyst at Bank Slaski brokerage.

The main market's all-share WIG index rose 0.3 percent to 15,933.6 points and turnover surged 80 percent to 287.6 million zlotys ($87.2) on both markets. Gainers led losers by 59 to 25 with 24 stocks flat.
Analysts said large-cap KGHM might still have some upside potential despite its relatively high market ratios.
They said the overall market should flatten out next week though some still saw upside potential.

"With the sales of Handlowy and KGHM it's evident there's still interest in the Polish market and Poles too will be careful about selling shares," said Kamil Kalemba, a trader at ING Baring Securities.
Analysts said Handlowy, which fell 1.2 percent on the back of Wednesday's 2.1 percent dip, should continue stabilising after its six-session rise since starting trade.
They said industrial boilermaker Rafako, down 3.7 percent in moderate trade, extended Wednesday's fall on investor concerns about the flooding affecting the southern town of Raciborz.
